research.website_note: The results describe Ramp at ramp.com, a financial operations platform for businesses.

strategy.observation: Ramp is an all-in-one financial operations platform used by 70,000+ businesses to manage cards, expenses, bill pay, travel, procurement, vendor management, banking, and accounting automation, and it claims customers save both money and time with its controls and automation.
strategy.offer_link: Because Ramp’s product touches many spend workflows, expense policy templates for mid-size finance teams could work as a practical content asset that helps prospects define controls around those workflows and gives the content team a concrete, utility-driven piece to publish or gate.
hypotheses: Ramp’s content team may want educational assets that attract finance and operations buyers.
Ramp may see policy-oriented content as useful for demand generation or product education.
Mid-size finance teams may be a meaningful audience segment for Ramp’s content, even though that is not stated in the facts.
strategy.angle: Ramp already covers cards, expenses, bill pay, travel, and reimbursements, so I thought a template pack for expense policies in mid-size finance teams could be a useful content asset for the workflows your buyers have to set up.
strategy.fit_reason: There is a plausible connection because Ramp sells spend-management software and the Head of Content could use policy templates as a buyer-facing asset. But the offer is generic and we do not know that this audience segment or content format is a priority for Ramp, so the fit is only a stretch.

draft.subject: Expense policy templates
draft.body:
Ramp already covers cards, expenses, bill pay, travel, and reimbursements.

That makes expense policy templates for mid-size finance teams a practical content asset. The idea is to give teams a simple way to set controls across the workflows Ramp already supports.

If helpful, I can send a few template outlines you could turn into a post or gated download. Worth a look?
